english.title: Owner / master of ship go / attempt to go to sea without the officers / seamen as required by s.47
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were the

(A)_[owner]_
(B)_[master]_

of a ship, namely **(..SPECIFY SHIP..), which

(C)_[went]_
(D)_[attempted to go]_

to sea without carrying such

(E)_[officers]_
(F)_[seamen]_
(G)_[officers and seamen]_

as it was required to carry under section 47 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995 in that **(..SPECIFY NATURE OF DEFICIENCY..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 49 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
owner / master of ship
go / attempt to go to sea
without the officers and/or seamen
as required by s.47

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence is subject to a ship or description of ship being made subject to an order of exemption by the Secretary of State under section 48 of the Act
(ii) The ship, if in the United Kingdom, may be detained

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
